name: Stryker Corporation

profile.description: Stryker Corporation is a leading global medical technology company offering innovative products and services in MedSurg and Neurotechnology, and Orthopaedics that help improve patient and hospital outcomes. The company operates through two segments: MedSurg and Neurotechnology (surgical instruments, endoscopy, patient handling, neurovascular devices) and Orthopaedics and Spine (hip and knee implants, trauma and extremities products, spine solutions, and the Mako robotic-arm assisted surgery platform). Stryker impacts more than 150 million patients annually worldwide.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Stryker turned the $1.6B Mako acquisition — a loss-making robotics business many customers and investors called unnecessary — into the platform that reshaped orthopaedics, and annual sales roughly tripled over Kevin Lobo's 14-year tenure to $25.1B in FY2025 [4][3]; this is a significant pivot within medtech rather than a whole-company reinvention. AI Deployment (1/2): Mako's CT-based planning and robotic guidance ship to customers, but Stryker does not quantify AI-specific revenue or internal AI savings, and leadership materials frame its innovation legacy around robotics and M&A rather than AI [4][8]. Market Share (2/2): Q2 2026 organic growth of ~9.0% was almost entirely procedure volume, with adjusted operating margin up 170bps to 27.4%, consistent with share gains in knees, trauma/extremities and neurovascular [1]. Pipeline (2/2): Mako RPS and expanding Mako applications plus FY2026 guidance of 8.3-9.3% organic growth give specific, dated visibility [1][8]. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D was $1.58B, or ~6.3% of FY2025 revenue (6.4% TTM), below the ~7-8% typical of large-cap medtech peers [3].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): 'Together with our customers, we are driven to make healthcare better' is specific and has demonstrably shaped strategy — Lobo is credited with shaping this mission alongside Stryker's specialized divisional operating model [4][8]. Community Impact (1/2): Stryker runs corporate giving and employee-matching programs, but no distinctive foundation-scale program with disclosed dollar amounts surfaced in research. Employee Retention (1/2): A board-planned CEO succession (COO Spencer Stiles to become CEO January 1, 2027, with Lobo as executive chair) shows deep internal bench and continuity, but no turnover or tenure statistics were found [4]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful open-market insider purchases were identified over the past 12 months.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Dividend stock (12 weight units): weighted sum 11.67/12 = 9.72, rounded to 10. D/E of 62.3% scores 1.0 and ROE of 16.4% scores 1.0 [3]. TTM revenue growth of 8.5% ($25.84B vs $23.82B) scores 0.95, and the 5-year revenue CAGR of 11.8% ($14.35B in 2020 to $25.12B in 2025) scores 1.0 [3]. Forward P/E of ~20.1 ($301.42 / $15.03 midpoint of FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $14.95-$15.10) scores 1.0, while the 14.4% TTM GAAP net margin is the lone drag at 0.72 [1][3]. Dividend metrics are all full marks: payout ratio 35.3% (1.0), 30+ consecutive years paid and raised (1.0 at 2x and 1.0), and ~6.9% 5-year dividend CAGR ($0.63 to $0.88 quarterly) (1.0 at 2x) [3]. Liquidity cleared easily: ~2.65M shares x $301.42 = ~$798M daily.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Stryker's revenue comes from physical implants, surgical robots, instruments, beds and neurovascular devices that require FDA clearance, sterile manufacturing and surgeon training — AI cannot substitute for a knee implant or a thrombectomy catheter, and Q2 2026 growth was driven by procedure volumes, not pricing [1]. The real 2026 technology risk was operational, not disruptive: a March 11, 2026 wiper attack by Iran-linked group Handala materially disrupted ordering and distribution and hurt Q1 results [2][6]. AI Opportunity (1/1): Mako's image-based planning and robotic guidance are revenue-generating, AI-enabled products embedded in Stryker's fastest-growing orthopaedic lines [8].

infinite_game.summary: Stryker plays a mostly infinite game in medtech: it held to a 'make healthcare better' cause through a decade-plus of robotics investment and has engineered an orderly, board-planned CEO succession for January 2027 [4]. Courage shows in the derided $1.6B Mako bet that became its growth engine, but its competitive language centers on share gains and acquisitive growth, and the 2026 cyberattack exposed operational fragility [2][4].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'Together with our customers, we are driven to make healthcare better' is service-oriented and has shaped real decisions such as the specialized divisional model and robotics investment [4][8]. It falls short of Sinek's top tier because the cause is largely shared across medtech and the company's identity is still defined by acquisition-led portfolio building.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The board planned the succession with Lobo, promoting COO Spencer Stiles from within — a sign of leadership continuity and bench strength [4]. However, the company's employees were exposed in the March 2026 cyber incident, prompting employee lawsuits (later withdrawn), and no hard retention data was found [6][7].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Stryker's investor messaging emphasizes outgrowing the market and taking share, with no evident framing of rivals like Zimmer Biomet or Medtronic as teachers; competition is treated as a contest to win [1][5].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Stryker has repeatedly reshaped its portfolio — robotics via Mako, neurovascular and peripheral vascular via acquisitions — but these are adjacent extensions of a device-maker model rather than an abandonment of the core business [4].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (2/2): Soon after becoming CEO, Lobo backed the $1.6B purchase of Mako, a loss-making robotics company many customers, investors and experts thought unnecessary, and kept investing until it reshaped orthopaedics [4]. Stryker continued to fund large strategic bets in 2025-2026 while absorbing a material cyberattack, keeping FY2026 organic growth guidance at 8.3-9.3% [1][2].

investment_thesis: Stryker is a best-in-class medtech compounder: FY2025 revenue reached $25.1B (11.8% 5-year CAGR), Q2 2026 delivered ~9.0% volume-driven organic growth with adjusted operating margin up 170bps to 27.4%, and management guides FY2026 adjusted EPS to $14.95-$15.10 [1][3]. The balance sheet is conservative (D/E 62%), the dividend has been raised for 30+ years at a 35% payout, and Mako robotics provides a durable installed-base moat that is structurally immune to AI substitution [3][8].
thesis_continued: The bear case: at ~31x trailing GAAP earnings and ~20x FY2026 guidance, the stock prices in uninterrupted high-single-digit growth while Q3 2026 faces a tough 9.5% organic comparison, an ongoing ~70-80bps peripheral vascular supply drag and softer hip volumes [5]. The March 2026 Handala cyberattack materially hurt Q1 and showed operational fragility, and a CEO transition to Spencer Stiles on January 1, 2027 adds execution uncertainty around a legacy tied closely to Lobo [2][4].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 earnings (late October 2026) against consensus of ~$6.68B revenue and $3.60 adjusted EPS; a beat on top of a 9.5% organic comparison would validate the 8.3-9.3% FY2026 organic guide [5]
Resolution of the peripheral vascular supply constraint that cost ~70-80bps of growth in Q2 2026, unlocking the vascular franchise as a growth contributor in 2027 [5]
Smooth handoff to CEO Spencer Stiles on January 1, 2027 with continued Mako platform expansion (Mako RPS and new applications) [4][8]
key_risks: Repeat of the March 2026 Iran-linked wiper attack that materially disrupted manufacturing, ordering and distribution systems and depressed Q1 2026 revenue (missed estimates by ~4.8%) [2][5][6]
Valuation risk at ~31x trailing GAAP P/E if procedure volumes normalize from post-pandemic highs or hip volumes keep softening [3][5]
Leadership transition risk as 14-year CEO Kevin Lobo, architect of the Mako strategy, moves to executive chair effective January 1, 2027 [4]
